item.text:
**Upgrades 24–28 are the five HVAC demand flexibility measures** in ResStock 2025 Release 1. They differ in when the thermostat changes, the size of the temperature offset, and how long preconditioning lasts. The release’s [Upgrade Measures page](https://natlabrockies.github.io/ResStock.github.io/docs/upgrade_measures.html) lists all five.

| Upgrade | Measure | Thermostat action |
|---|---|---|
| **24** | On-peak load shedding, **2°F offset** | For the **4-hour peak window**, lower the heating setpoint or raise the cooling setpoint by 2°F. |
| **25** | **4-hour** pre-peak load shifting, **2°F offset** | Preheat or precool by 2°F for the 4 hours immediately before the peak window. |
| **26** | On-peak load shedding, **4°F offset** | Same timing as 24, with a larger 4°F adjustment. |
| **27** | **4-hour** pre-peak load shifting, **4°F offset** | Same timing as 25, with a larger 4°F preconditioning adjustment. |
| **28** | **1-hour** pre-peak load shifting, **2°F offset** | Same offset as 25, but preconditions for only 1 hour. |

These settings are documented in [*HVAC Load Flexibility*, Table 8, p. 25](https://docs.nlr.gov/docs/fy26osti/93846.pdf#page=33).

**Shedding** reduces demand during the peak by allowing indoor temperatures to drift toward less comfortable settings. **Shifting** uses energy earlier to store heating or cooling in the building. The final shifting measures have **no on-peak setpoint adjustment**; they do not combine preconditioning with shedding. Peak windows vary by state and season. See [the report, §§1.2.1–1.2.4 and 4.4](https://docs.nlr.gov/docs/fy26osti/93846.pdf).

The modeled dispatch occurs nearly every day to estimate technical potential, so annual energy savings should not be interpreted as those of a typical demand-response program. [Report, §1.2.5, p. 7](https://docs.nlr.gov/docs/fy26osti/93846.pdf#page=15).
